profile.reading:
This record covers an Optimum owned site on Centennial Avenue in the Possumtown section of Piscataway Township, Middlesex County, New Jersey. Optimum is the residential and business broadband, television and phone brand of Altice USA, a publicly traded telecommunications company headquartered in Long Island, New York. Altice USA formed in 2016 when the European telecom group Altice acquired Cablevision Systems Corporation and Suddenlink Communications and combined their networks. The Optimum brand descends from the older Cablevision service, which built out cable infrastructure across the New York metropolitan area, including central and northern New Jersey, over several decades.

Neither Altice USA nor Optimum publishes an address specific description of what this Centennial Avenue site does. Cable operators of this scale typically run a layered network of large regional hub facilities, smaller local headends, and network operations space that handles video, broadband and telephone traffic for a defined service area, and a Piscataway location would fit naturally into that role given the township's position within Optimum's core central New Jersey footprint. Nothing in the public record identifies this specific site as a customer facing data center or colocation facility open to outside tenants, and it more plausibly serves as internal network infrastructure supporting the surrounding Middlesex County service area rather than as a commercial data center comparable to the wholesale and retail colocation facilities elsewhere in this registry.

Middlesex County property records place the site within a commercial and industrial section of Piscataway Township, an area that also hosts corporate offices, life sciences companies and other data center and colocation facilities given its position along the Route 1 corridor between New Brunswick and the New Jersey Turnpike, but no permit filing, zoning case or news coverage specific to this Centennial Avenue address describing the building's construction, power capacity or cooling systems was found.

Telecommunications companies generally treat the technical details of network hub and headend facilities as operationally sensitive rather than public marketing material, unlike wholesale colocation providers who compete for tenants by publishing power and space specifications, and that industry norm is a more likely explanation for the absence of published detail here than any unusual secrecy specific to this site.

reading.body:
This facility in Piscataway Township, Middlesex County is mapped but publishes no power capacity, no square footage, and no IT specifications. Searches of the operator's own site and public sources yield no facility-specific detail beyond the address. The operator Optimum Communications (Altice USA) publishes capacity only for other locations, not this one.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities, of which 5 publish power figures totaling 111.3 MW. This Optimum campus would rank sixth in the state by published capacity if its specifications were disclosed, but because no figures are public it cannot be sized against peers or compared to the state's known load.

Without published specs, this site's relevance to AI infrastructure cannot be assessed. It may be a legacy telecom facility, an edge location, or positioned for cloud workloads, but the operator has chosen not to disclose the capacity that would place it in the grid constraint conversation.
